alt: Top: an open pit dug through overburden down to a deposit, with stepped benches on the walls and a waste heap beside it. Bottom: strip mining of a flat seam; after the seam is taken from one strip, overburden from the next strip is dumped into the gap.
caption: Surface methods remove the overburden and dig the deposit out from above.

alt: Cross-section of a vertical shaft from a headframe at the surface down to an inclined ore body, with horizontal tunnels that follow the ore. The ground above old workings has sunk. A note lists the benefits and risks of underground mining.
caption: Underground mining disturbs less land but costs more and is riskier for miners.

alt: Two flow rows. Phytomining: plants grown on low-grade ore absorb metal compounds, are harvested and burned, and metal is extracted from the ash. Bioleaching: bacteria break down low-grade ore, releasing metal compounds into a leachate from which the metal is recovered. Benefits and limitations are listed below.
caption: Phytomining uses plants; bioleaching uses bacteria; both suit low-grade ore.

after: ## Factors in the decision to extract
alt: Eight factors in three groups feed one decision. Physical: exploration, geology, accessibility and terrain, climate. Deposit: quantity and quality (ore grade). Economic and environmental: supply and demand, cost and profit, and the environmental impact assessment. A mine opens only if it should make a profit and its impacts are acceptable.
caption: Profit and acceptable impacts decide; the eight factors feed into both.

alt: A timeline from before mining (exploration, EIA, restoration plan) through extraction to after closure. Two panels list the options for the land: restoration by replacing overburden, soil improvement, bioremediation and tree planting; or repurposing as landfill, lakes, recreation or nature reserves.
caption: Plan and fund restoration before mining starts, or it may never happen.

alt: Bar chart of ore needed for 60 tonnes of copper: 5,000 tonnes from deposit X at 1.2% grade and 15,000 tonnes from deposit Y at 0.4% grade, three times as much rock.
caption: A lower grade means more rock dug, moved and processed for each tonne of metal.
